originalTitle: '101-year-old great-grandmother' arrested for selling cannabis in Nigeria
title: Grandma Esther's Big Surprise: A Special Plant Story from Nigeria!
content:
Hello, my wonderful friends across Africa! Your kid-friendly news reporter is here with an interesting story from Nigeria. Imagine someone who has lived for 101 whole years! That's a super-duper long time, isn't it? Well, this story is about a very old lady named Grandma Esther. She is a great-grandmother, which means she has seen many, many birthdays and lots of happy families grow up around her. But something surprising happened to her, and it teaches us about rules and safety. Let's find out together!

Meet Grandma Esther!

Grandma Esther Ogunmabo is 101 years old. Can you imagine having 101 candles on your birthday cake? That's more candles than you can count on all your fingers and toes! Being 101 means she has lived through so much history, seen so many changes, and probably has so many amazing stories to tell. She is a 'great-grandmother', which means she is the grandma of someone's grandma. Wow! That means she has a big, big family. Living for over a hundred years is very special and not many people get to do it. Did you know? If you are seven years old, Grandma Esther has lived 94 more years than you! That’s like living your whole life over and over again many times!

What Happened to Grandma Esther?

This very old and special lady had a bit of a surprise. The police in Nigeria came to talk to her. They said she was selling something called 'cannabis'. It's a type of plant. They found small packets of a strong kind of this plant, sometimes called 'skunk', and they believed she was selling them. Because of this, the police took her to ask her some questions. This might sound a little bit scary, but it's how the police find out what really happened when rules are broken.

What is this 'Special Plant' (Cannabis)?

So, what is cannabis? Well, it's a plant! Just like the plants you see in your garden or in the fields. But this plant is different from a pretty flower or a delicious vegetable. Cannabis is a plant that has special parts that can make people feel very funny or even unwell if they use it the wrong way. It's not like food or regular medicine. In many places, including our country Nigeria, it is against the rules, or 'illegal', to sell this plant because it can be harmful to people, especially children and young people. Did you know? There are thousands of different plants in the world! Some plants give us tasty fruits and vegetables, some give us wood for building houses, and some are used to make special medicines by doctors. But some plants can be dangerous if they are not used correctly or without strict rules.

Why Are There Rules About Plants Like This?

We have rules for many things, don't we? We have rules at school, rules at home, and rules for playing games. These rules help to keep us safe and make sure everyone gets along. Countries also have rules, called 'laws'. These laws are made by grown-ups in the government to keep everyone in the country safe and healthy. For a plant like cannabis, the rules say you cannot sell it because it can make people feel very strange, or even sick, and can cause problems for their health and their lives. Think about it like this: some sweets are okay to eat a little bit of, but if you eat too many, you might get a tummy ache! This plant is even more serious. It's like a warning sign on something that isn't safe for everyone, especially children. Did you know? Just like we have traffic rules to keep drivers and walkers safe, countries have laws about certain plants and substances to protect their citizens from harm. It's all about keeping our communities healthy and peaceful.

What Happens Next When Rules are Broken?

When someone is accused of breaking a rule, especially a big one like selling a plant that isn't allowed, the police need to find out all the facts. This is called an 'investigation'. They will ask questions, gather information, and try to understand everything that happened. Sometimes, a judge in a 'court' (a special place where rules are discussed) will listen to everyone and decide what is fair and what should happen next. It's important that everyone, no matter how old they are, follows the laws of the land.

What Can We Learn From This Story?

This story about Grandma Esther teaches us some important things. First, it reminds us that rules are there to keep us safe and healthy. It's always important to know the rules of your country and listen to the grown-ups who teach you about them. Second, it shows that even very old people can sometimes get into trouble if they don't follow the laws. And third, it reminds us to be curious but also careful about things we don't understand. If you ever see a plant or something strange and you are not sure what it is, always ask a trusted grown-up! Did you know? Asking questions when you don't understand something is a very smart thing to do! It helps you learn and stay safe! So, that's our story about Grandma Esther and the special plant. Let's all remember to follow the rules, stay safe, and always be curious about the world around us!
summary: 101-year-old great-grandmother Esther Ogunmabo was questioned by police in Nigeria for allegedly selling a special plant called cannabis, reminding us all about the importance of following rules and staying safe.
whyMatters: This story matters because it teaches us that rules (or 'laws') are important for everyone, no matter how old they are, to keep people safe and healthy, especially from plants or things that can be harmful.

originalTitle: Iran faces 'greatest financial offensive ever', says US treasury secretary
title: Countries, Money, and Friends: A Big Choice!
content:
Hello, Super Friends!

Hello, everyone! It's me, your friendly news reporter from Africa! I'm so happy to share some big news with you today. News helps us learn about the world, even faraway places! Let's go on an adventure to learn about countries and friends and how they work together. It's like a big puzzle where everyone has a piece!

A Big Story From Far Away

Today, we're talking about two big countries. One is called America, and it's very, very far away. The other is called Iran, and it's also very far from us. What these two countries are doing is a big story. It's like when friends have a disagreement in the playground. Sometimes, big countries have disagreements too.

What is America Doing?

America has said something very important. They said they will stop all "money business" with Iran. Can you imagine that? It's a very big decision! This means America won't buy things from Iran anymore. And America won't sell things to Iran either. It's like saying, "We are not going to share our toys or sweets with you for a while." This is a very serious thing for countries to do. It means they are not being "money friends" anymore. They are putting a pause on helping each other with goods.

What Does "Money Business" Mean?

"Money business" is how countries help each other get things. It means they sell things to each other and buy things from each other. We also call this "trade." For example, one country might grow a lot of yummy fruit. Another country might make cool toys. They trade so everyone can have fruit and toys! When countries do "money business," they give each other money for these things. This helps people get the food they need, the clothes they wear, and the cars they drive. Did you know? Countries trade all sorts of things! From yummy fruit like bananas to big machines and even special medicines. It helps everyone have more choices!

Why is This Happening?

America is doing this because they are not happy with Iran. Sometimes, countries don't agree on things. It's a bit like when you and your friend might have different ideas about playing a game. America wants Iran to do some things differently. So, America is using this "no money business" rule. They hope it will make Iran think about what they are doing and change. It's a way for countries to talk to each other without using mean words. They use rules about money instead.

Choosing Friends

This is where the story gets even bigger for other countries around the world. America also said something else very important. They said, "If any other country does money business with Iran, then America won't do money business with *them*!" Wow! That's a big choice, isn't it? It's like saying to your friends, "You have to choose who you want to play with today!"

What About Other Countries?

Imagine a country called Banana Land. Banana Land loves to sell its yummy bananas to Iran. And Banana Land also loves to sell its yummy bananas to America. Now, Banana Land has a problem. If Banana Land keeps selling bananas to Iran, America might say, "No more bananas from you, Banana Land! We won't buy from you anymore!" So, Banana Land has to choose. Will it keep its money friendship with Iran and maybe lose America's friendship? Or will it stop selling to Iran to keep America as a money friend? It's a very big decision for Banana Land and for all the other countries in the world. They have to think very carefully. Did you know? There are almost 200 countries in the world! Each one has to make its own choices about who to be friends with and who to trade with.

Making Big Choices

Countries have to think about what is best for their people. They need to think about jobs for their mums and dads. They need to think about getting enough food and other important things for everyone. If they choose to stop business with America, they might lose a lot of money and not be able to get many things. If they choose to stop business with Iran, they might lose money there too. It's a tough spot to be in! It's like when you have two friends, and they are not getting along. You want to be kind to everyone, but sometimes you have to choose which game to play or who to sit next to at lunch.

Did You Know? Fun Facts!

Did you know that "money business" can also be called "economics"? It's a big word for how countries earn and spend money and how they share things! Did you know that when countries are good friends and trade lots, it can help everyone get along better? Sharing is caring, even for big countries! Did you know that Africa is a continent with many, many countries? And all these countries trade with each other and with countries far away! We are all connected by buying and selling things. Did you know that the people who help countries with their money are sometimes called "treasury secretaries"? They are like the big money bosses for a country!

So What Happens Next?

Now, everyone will watch to see what happens next. Will Iran change what America wants? Will other countries choose to stop money business with Iran to keep America happy? Or will they keep doing business with Iran and face America's new rules? It's like watching a very big game unfold, and we don't know who will win or what the score will be. This story is about how countries talk to each other. Sometimes they talk nicely. Sometimes they have big disagreements. And sometimes, like now, they make big rules about money to try and make things change.

Keep Smiling, Little Stars!

That's all the big news for today, my super friends! Remember to always be kind to your friends. And try to understand when people or countries have different ideas. Learning about the world is exciting! Keep asking questions and stay curious. And remember, even faraway news can teach us about being good friends. See you next time!
summary: America has announced it will stop all money business with Iran, and any other country that continues to trade with Iran will also be cut off by America.
whyMatters: This is important because countries need to trade and be friends to get the things they need, and these big choices can change how countries work together and help each other.
